subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to the existing retention rules and report them in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The implementation is the narrow code-path fix, but accepting physical removal of retained session artifacts intersects broader archive-retention policy that automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the supplied CLI proof.

options.title: Ask for broader upgrade proof
options.body: Pause for a large real-store or upgrade-style cleanup transcript if maintainers want more evidence before changing operator cleanup behavior.

options.title: Defer to retention policy work
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want the archive naming/no-delete/config policy settled before changing cleanup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as-is if maintainers accept removing stale deleted/reset archives under the existing retention rules and the supplied CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the sessions cleanup UX and maintenance controls that define this operator-visible cleanup boundary.
